back: RLVR uses a programmatic, verifiable reward (answer checker, tests); RLHF uses a learned reward model trained on human preferences.
A sampled completion (full chain of thought plus answer) for a prompt; GRPO samples a group of G per prompt.
grad J = E[r(y) * grad log pi(y)], with log pi(y) the SUM of token log-probabilities of the sequence.

front: Why a baseline does not bias the gradient
back: E[b grad log pi] = b * grad(sum pi) = 0 for any b independent of the sample; it only reduces variance.
A_i = (r_i - mean(r)) / (std(r) + eps) over the G rollouts of one prompt (sample std, ddof = 1).
With k of G correct: sigma = sqrt(k(G-k)/(G(G-1))); correct rollouts get (1-k/G)/sigma, wrong ones -(k/G)/sigma.

front: When are all GRPO advantages zero?
back: When all rollouts of a prompt have the same reward (all right or all wrong): no learning signal from that prompt.
L = -(1/G) sum_i A_i * sum_t log pi(y_t | x, y_<t), advantages detached.
-(1/G) sum_i min(rho_i A_i, clip(rho_i, 1-eps, 1+eps) A_i), rho = pi_theta / pi_old; zero gradient when the clipped term is strictly smaller.

front: Why the loss value is 0 at the first step
back: Ratio = 1 and advantages sum to zero give a zero scalar loss, but the gradient A_i * grad log pi is not zero.
beta * mean(logp - ref_logp) against a frozen reference model; needs a second model copy and can destabilise training when computed on summed log-probs.

front: Correctness reward with a required box
back: Reward 1 only if the last boxed answer is verified: the box requirement is an implicit format reward.
format_reward *= correctness_reward so that formatting pays only for correct answers; avoids wrong-but-tagged outputs tying with right ones.
p^G + (1-p)^G for success probability p and G independent rollouts (0.17 for p = 0.2, G = 8).
